findings.issue: The app ships no test runner, no test script and zero test files; every pure function and load function is unguarded once the acceptance suite is retired.
findings.suggestion: Add vitest with unit tests for src/lib/utils.js and the +page.server.js load functions (they're pure-ish and easy to cover with mocked api responses).

findings.issue: humanize/englishName/latestFlavor/idFromUrl/dexNumber are untested transformation helpers used on every page; a regex or capitalization refactor breaks names and flavor text silently.
findings.suggestion: Table-driven unit tests with real API edge cases: 'mr-mime', 'thunder-punch', flavor text containing \f, URLs without trailing slash.

findings.issue: Pagination math and the page clamp (`Math.min(pageParam, totalPages)`, NaN/garbage input via `|| 1` at :8) are untested; an off-by-one would still pass acceptance tests that only sample pages 1 and 2.
findings.suggestion: Unit-test the load against ?page=0, ?page=999, ?page=abc and boundary counts (e.g. exactly 48 matches).

findings.issue: speciesFromPokemonRefs' alternate-form boundary (pokemonId >= 10000), dedup-by-species and augment mutation are untested; inverting the comparison silently re-admits Mega forms.
findings.suggestion: Unit-test with a ref list containing ids 386, 10033 and duplicate species, asserting dex order and dedup.

findings.issue: The hidden flag is OR-accumulated via index alignment between entries and the mapped refs; any refactor of the map breaks the alignment and marks the wrong species as hidden.
findings.suggestion: Test with an ability whose pokemon list mixes hidden and non-hidden entries for the same species.

findings.issue: Sorting semantics — missing values last in both directions, tiebreaks, aria-sort flip at :84 — are guarded only by one acceptance scenario.
findings.suggestion: Component test asserting row order (and aria-sort) for ascending/descending clicks on a table containing null power/accuracy rows.

findings.issue: Hand-rolled concurrency limiter (waiter queue, finally release) is untested; a refactor can deadlock or starve waiters under the 100+ record fan-outs this app does.
findings.suggestion: Unit-test with a mock fetch and MAX_CONCURRENT assertions, or replace with a small well-tested utility.

findings.issue: URL-state sync (param omission in queryString, debounce race, afterNavigate typed-reset) is untested; rapid typing or a lost default-omission would corrupt the URL.
findings.suggestion: Test that queryString omits empty/default params and that filter changes reset page to 1.

findings.issue: A single missing Pokémon record escalates to error(500) and kills the whole home list instead of degrading; no test covers partial API failure.
findings.suggestion: Either test the failure path explicitly or degrade by skipping the card and logging.

findings.issue: 404 responses return null without caching, so every not-found request re-hits the API; the perf characteristic is untested and invisible.
findings.suggestion: Cache nulls too (data is a fixed snapshot) and note it in a test of the api client.

summary: The app contains no tests of its own: no runner, no script, no spec files. All data transformation, filtering, pagination, sorting and error handling is guarded solely by the external acceptance suite. The codebase is unusually unit-testable (pure helpers in lib/utils.js, thin load functions), so the omission is a straightforward gap to close before anyone refactors the data layer.
